'''Motilal Madan''' (born 1 January 1939<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.naasindia.org/fdetail.html#M001 | title=National Academy of Agricultural Sciences | access-date=29 December 2011 | archive-date=8 August 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170808061319/http://naasindia.org/fdetail.html#M001 | url-status=dead }}</ref>) is an Indian [[biotechnology]] researcher, [[veterinarian]], [[Academic staff|academic]] and administrator. In a career spanning over 35 years, Madan published 432 research articles and policy papers in international and national reference journals—including 226 original research papers—and pioneered research in [[Reproductive endocrinology and infertility|reproductive endocrinology]], embryo biotechnology, [[In vitro fertilisation]], and [[cloning]].<ref name="ndri-srs">
{{cite web|title=Alumni Association of NDRI-SRS: Illustrious Alumni|url=http://alumnindribng.org/history/IllustriousAlumni/illustriousalumni.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040721204419/http://www.alumnindribng.org/History/IllustriousAlumni/illustriousalumni.html|archive-date=2004-07-21|work=Alumni Association of the Southern Regional Station of National Dairy Research Institute|accessdate=2007-03-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/chandigarh/haryana-padma-shri-for-neeraj-chopra-sumit-antil-7741878/|title = Haryana: Padma Shri for Neeraj Chopra, Sumit Antil|date = 26 January 2022|newspaper=The Indian Express|accessdate=11 August 2026}}</ref>

From 1987 to 1994, Madan served as Project Director of Embryo Transfer Technology at India's premier dairy research institute, the [[National Dairy Research Institute]] (NDRI).<ref name="ndri-srs" />  He led a research team at the institute that performed the first successful in vitro fertilisation of a buffalo in the world, leading to the birth of a calf, named "Pratham", in November 1990.<ref>Having successfully implemented several animal biotechnology paradigms in Indian Agriculture,  Madan is considered a pioneer in the field of Animal Reproductive Biotechnology in India. Due to immense contributions to the Indian Agriculture through animal biotechniques. Madan is considered the "Father of Animal Biotech Revolution" in India.
{{cite conference|last=Madan|first=Moti Lal|author2=S.K. Singla|author3=S. Jailkhani|author4=J.D. Ambrose|year=1991|title=In vitro fertilization in buffaloes and birth of test tube buffalo calf 'Pratham'|conference=World Buffalo Congress|conference-url=http://www.wbc2007.org/|book-title=Proceedings of the III World Buffalo Congress}}</ref>

From 1994 to 1995, Madan served as the Director (Research) of the NDRI in [[Karnal]] and was later, from 1995 to 1999, the Deputy Director General (Animal Science) of the [[Indian Council of Agricultural Research]]. In November 2006 he became Vice-Chancellor of the [[U.P. Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Veterinary Science University and Cattle Research Institute|Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Veterinary Science University]], [[Mathura, Uttar Pradesh|Mathura]]. Earlier he served as the Vice Chancellor of [[Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth]] in [[Akola city|Akola]].<ref>
{{cite news 
 | first = Yoginder
 | last = Gupta
 | title = Madan takes over as VC of vet varsity 
 | url = https://www.tribuneindia.com/2006/20061112/haryana.htm#9
 | work = [[The Tribune (Chandigarh)|The Tribune]]
 | date = 2006-11-11
 | access-date = 2007-08-14}}</ref>

Madan was conferred the prestigious [[Padma Shri]], the fourth highest civilian award in the [[India|Republic of India]], by the [[Government of India]] in January 2022 for distinguished service in the fields of science and engineering. While congratulating him, [[Haryana]] Chief Minister [[Manohar Lal Khattar]] commented that "Madan's accomplishments have brought pride to the country."<ref>{{Cite tweet|title=Register|url-access=limited|user=mlkhattar|number=1486061918448402437|url=https://twitter.com/mlkhattar/status/1486061918448402437|access-date=2022-01-26|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-26|title=Haryana: Padma Shri for Neeraj Chopra, Sumit Antil|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/chandigarh/haryana-padma-shri-for-neeraj-chopra-sumit-antil-7741878/|access-date=2022-01-26|website=The Indian Express|language=en}}</ref>

==Early years and education==
Madan was born into a [[Kashmiri Pandits|Kashmiri Pandit]] family in [[Srinagar]] on 1 January 1939.<ref name="mlmadan.github.io">{{Cite web |last=Madan |first=Motilan |title=Curriculum Vitae of Dr. M. L. Madan |url=https://mlmadan.github.io/resume.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126034409/https://mlmadan.github.io/resume.pdf |website=ML Madan |access-date=26 January 2022 |archive-date=26 January 2022 |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref> He received his [[Bachelor of Veterinary Science|BVSc]] (Veterinary Medicine) degree from Punjab College of Veterinary Science & Animal Husbandry in 1959 with a gold medal, after which he obtained his [[Master of Veterinary Science|MVSc]] degree from the [[National Dairy Research Institute, Karnal]] with a gold medal in 1965.<ref name="mlmadan.github.io"/> He then obtained his doctoral ([[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]]) degree from the [[University of Missouri]], in 1971.<ref name="mlmadan.github.io"/>
